Background (from the session that started this one):
On 2026-11-10 JusPrin 2's server host jusprinv2.obico.io went live in production, and Kenneth smoke-tested it with a copy of the JusPrin 2 desktop app built from `jusprin-dev`, using its own scratch data folder. Two account displays in the app's Home page showed stale values while Preferences › Account showed the right ones. Production is the real server; the test account k@obico.io (production user 263741) has real credits, and creating new production accounts needs Kenneth to do it himself. Staging (jusprinv2-stg.obico.io, set `jusprin_server/base_url` in the app's settings file) is the place to reproduce.

Task:
Reproduce and, if real, fix two stale account displays in JusPrin 2's Home page (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/`, its backend `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/`).

1. Home's AI card ("Signed in as k@obico.io / 500 credits left / Sign-up credits 500 of 500 left") kept showing 500 credits after the account had spent credits: the server said 494 and then 488, and Preferences › Account and the Billing and usage page both showed the right number. Leaving a project and returning to Home did not refresh it. Find where Home's card gets the balance and when it refreshes, and decide whether it should update after a chat turn or on returning to Home.
2. The first-run page "Bring your printers from JusPrin 1?" said "Signed in as k+jusprinv2-smoke@obico.io" after that account had signed out and k@obico.io had signed in with Google (Preferences showed k@obico.io). Find where that line gets its email.

Reproduce each against staging, not production, following the repo's Bug Fix Policy (no fix without a reproduction) and `agent-docs/jusprin/` guidance. Done means: each display shows the current account and balance, with a test where the code allows one, on a branch from `jusprin-dev`; ask Kenneth before pushing.

name: ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33551592-d22c-4161-9a14-9a22ef798541
  modified: 2026-10-28T13:12:42.393Z
---

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

description: "Drive the real app signed in to a local gateway through an injected page script; which conf keys, why a copied binary dies, and what still needs the screen."
metadata:
  node_type: memory

---

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

**ONLY the exact allowed outputs listed per command are valid.** Anything else — gcloud auth errors, kubectl failures, tracebacks, empty output, unrecognized strings, timeouts — is an infrastructure failure. When it happens:


# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

Home still showed 494 after I opened a new project and came back. The cause is that Home asks the server for the balance only once per app run.
- **Old email on the JusPrin 1 import page:** the cause is that closing Preferences never sends Home a fresh copy of the account. So a sign-out or sign-in there doesn't show on Home until something else redraws it. I couldn't click Sign out in the real app: Preferences is a modal window, background clicks can't reach it, and two requests for full-screen control got no answer. Instead, the test harness that drives the real app from code will click the real Sign out button inside Preferences.
- **Fix, uncommitted on branch `claude/home-account-refresh`:** Home asks for the balance again each time it comes on screen and when Preferences closes. It drops the stored balance as soon as the signed-in email changes. Closing Preferences now redraws Home.
- **Test:** the first-launch harness mode now checks three things. The card shows the new balance after leaving Home and coming back. After Preferences signs out, the card no longer names the account.

Once the build finishes, I'll run the harness with the fix taken out to show both checks fail, then with it to show they pass. After that I'll check the real app against staging.

Branch `claude/home-account-refresh`, commit 4da941e553, worktree
/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/home-account-refresh (Release build in build/arm64).
Not pushed; waits on Kenneth.

## Causes
- OrcaHomeBackend fetched /ent/jusprin/v2/account once per app run (m_account_requested never reset),
  so the credits never changed and a later account inherited the earlier one's balance.
- ShellController::open_preferences never re-sent Home's state after the window closed, so a
  sign-out or sign-in in Preferences did not reach Home or the first-run import page until
  something else redrew Home.

## Fix
Credits are kept with the email they belong to (dropped and re-read when it changes), re-read each
time Home comes on screen, and re-read with a Home redraw when Preferences closes.

## Evidence
- Staging, real app, before the fix: k+stg-e2e1 showed "494 credits left" on Home; after one
  Standard request the server said 493; Home still said 494 after New project and back.
  Screenshot: scratchpad/evidence/credits-before-fix-home-494-server-493.jpg (session f7445e00).
- Shell harness --fresh-example (stand-in server): new checks fail without the fix (card still
  "Signed in as alex@example.com / 500 credits left" after the server dropped to 493 and after the
  real Preferences Sign out button was clicked) and pass with it. Default harness mode: 625 checks,
  0 failures. jusprin_tests: all 175 cases pass.

- The fixed build was not checked in the real app against staging: screen access to the fixed copy
  was refused / timed out, and clicks inside the modal Preferences window need full-screen control.
  Ready to run: scratchpad/Fixed.app with --datadir scratchpad/data3 (signed in to staging as
  k+stg-e2e1; that staging token expires 2026-11-11).

**Email on "Bring your printers from JusPrin 1?".** The line reads the signed-in email from the settings file, which was correct. But closing Preferences never told Home to redraw. So after a sign-out or a new sign-in in Preferences, Home and the first-run page kept showing whatever they last drew.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the clang-tidy check that gates pull requests (.github/workflows/clang_tidy.yml)
# on your branch, so its findings match what CI reports. Linux and macOS.
#
#   scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh            check your changes against OrcaSlicer's main
#   scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh --fix      also add the missing includes it names
#
# It configures a separate build directory (build-tidy) without the precompiled
# header, uses the clang-tidy on your system or installs the pinned one into a
# virtual environment inside it, and runs scripts/clang_tidy_diff.py the way CI
# does. Uncommitted changes are checked too.

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh [options]

  -b, --base REV       revision to compare against (default: main of the remote that
                       points at OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer, else origin/main)
      --no-fetch       do not fetch that remote's main first
  -B, --build-dir DIR  build directory for the compile database (default: build-tidy)
  -d, --deps-dir DIR   dependency build directory (default: deps/build on Linux,
                       deps/build/<arch> on macOS)
  -j, --jobs N         parallel clang-tidy runs (default: all cores)
      --fix            apply clang-tidy's fixes (adds the missing includes)
  -y, --yes            install missing tools without asking; another clang-tidy
                       version found on the system is then not offered
  -h, --help           show this help
EOF
}

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
cd "$ROOT"

BASE=""
FETCH=1
BUILD_DIR=build-tidy
DEPS_DIR=""
JOBS=""
FIX=0
YES=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        -b|--base) BASE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --no-fetch) FETCH=0; shift ;;
        -B|--build-dir) BUILD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -d|--deps-dir) DEPS_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -j|--jobs) JOBS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --fix) FIX=1; shift ;;
        -y|--yes) YES=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

case "$BUILD_DIR" in
    /*) ;;
    *) BUILD_DIR="$ROOT/$BUILD_DIR" ;;
esac

OS=$(uname -s)
case "$OS" in
    Linux) ;;
    Darwin) ;;
    *) echo "Unsupported system $OS. On Windows, use scripts/run_clang_tidy.ps1." >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

# Ask before installing anything. Without a terminal, or with "no", print the
# command instead so it can be run by hand.
ask() {
    [ "$YES" = 1 ] && return 0
    [ -t 0 ] || return 1
    local reply
    read -r -p "$1 [y/N] " reply
    [[ "$reply" =~ ^[Yy] ]]
}

Decided 2026-10-23 in a design session; the full document is the untracked `agent-setup-flow-decisions.md` in
the main checkout root (never committed). Context: JusPrin's own Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui as
641c17f13e (modal over any screen, Agent section draws the same key/tool rows as setup, shell reloads the docked
agent on close if `jusprin_agent` changed).

Kenneth's decisions:
1. Preferences › Agent is the one setup flow, first time included. The in-pane chooser, the printer panel's
   in-body chooser, the print-issue MessageDialog ("Set up now / Not now"), `open_agent_setup`/`request_setup`
   and `AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup` are to go. The first-run setup boards on the canvas page "Agent setup &
   Preferences" are history.
2. No separate question. Each surface shows its own not-set-up state with one action that opens Preferences ›
   Agent: the print-issue bubble draws one button "Set up the agent…" (Kenneth chose "agent" over "assistant") instead of Ask AI / Resolve with AI;
   the pane and printer panel keep their "No agent connected" offer and setup bar; calibration's board-3
   Confirmation adds one sentence and its primary button reads "Set up the agent…".
3. When the window closes with an agent, the surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent for the
   person (bubble shows its two buttons; confirmation's button becomes "Start test"; panel greeting continues).
4. Cancel changes nothing underneath; the pending choice stays where it was; the printer panel is never closed
   on the person's behalf.
5. The pane keeps its own entry (offer, setup bar, chat list row), each opening Preferences › Agent.

**Why:** three different answers to "needs the agent, none set up" existed and calibration would add a fourth;
Kenneth: "On the homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"
The Agent pane does not exist on Home (force-collapsed in `on_page_changed`), so only a window over Home works.

**How to apply:** any new entry point that needs the Agent follows rule 2 to 4; never add a chooser inside a
pane or a MessageDialog. Implementation detail noted: the printer panel builds its runtime at `open()` and must
reload it after Preferences closes. Related: [[calibration-design-decisions]], [[agent-setup-api-key-path]],
[[api-key-saved-state]], [[use-orca-messagedialog]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

Canvas (2026-10-23): board "Agent setup · one door" on the "Agent setup & Preferences" page and board 3b on "Calibration · Printer & Filament" draw these states; builder `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_no_agent_boards.py`. With no provider set up, the composer's model picker shows the raw id "gpt-5.4-mini" (default provider openai, empty catalogue) and no thinking picker; Kenneth asked for it drawn.

# --- clang-tidy ---------------------------------------------------------------

REQUIREMENTS="$ROOT/scripts/clang_tidy_requirements.txt"
PINNED=$(sed -n 's/^clang-tidy==//p' "$REQUIREMENTS")
VENV="$BUILD_DIR/clang-tidy-venv"

is_pinned() {
    [ -x "$1" ] && "$1" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "version $PINNED"
}

CLANG_TIDY="${CLANG_TIDY:-}"
if [ -n "$CLANG_TIDY" ]; then
    # Set by the caller: use it as is.
    is_pinned "$CLANG_TIDY" || echo "Warning: $CLANG_TIDY is not clang-tidy $PINNED, so results may differ from CI." >&2
else
    # One already on the system comes first: the pinned version outright, another
    # version if the user accepts the difference. The pinned version is installed
    # into a virtual environment otherwise.
    INSTALLED=""
    for candidate in $(command -v clang-tidy "clang-tidy-${PINNED%%.*}" || true) \
                     "/usr/lib/llvm-${PINNED%%.*}/bin/clang-tidy" \
                     "$(brew --prefix llvm 2>/dev/null || true)/bin/clang-tidy"; do
        if is_pinned "$candidate"; then
            CLANG_TIDY="$candidate"
            break
        fi
        [ -z "$INSTALLED" ] && [ -x "$candidate" ] && INSTALLED="$candidate"
    done
    if [ -z "$CLANG_TIDY" ] && [ -n "$INSTALLED" ] && [ "$YES" = 0 ] && ! is_pinned "$VENV/bin/clang-tidy"; then
        echo "Found $INSTALLED, which is $("$INSTALLED" --version | sed -n 's/.*version \([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1), not the $PINNED CI uses, so results may differ slightly."
        if ask "Use it anyway?"; then
            CLANG_TIDY="$INSTALLED"
        fi
    fi
fi
if [ -z "$CLANG_TIDY" ]; then
    CLANG_TIDY="$VENV/bin/clang-tidy"
    if ! is_pinned "$CLANG_TIDY"; then
        if ask "clang-tidy $PINNED (the version CI uses) is not installed. Install it into $VENV?"; then
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
            if ! python3 -m venv "$VENV"; then
                echo "Could not create a Python virtual environment." >&2
                [ "$OS" = Linux ] && echo "On Debian or Ubuntu, install it with: sudo apt-get install -y python3-venv" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            "$VENV/bin/pip" install --quiet --upgrade pip
            "$VENV/bin/pip" install --quiet -r "$REQUIREMENTS"
        else
            echo "To install it yourself, run:" >&2
            echo "    python3 -m venv $VENV && $VENV/bin/pip install -r scripts/clang_tidy_requirements.txt" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
fi

# --- Dependencies -------------------------------------------------------------

# A configured build directory remembers where its dependencies are.
if [ -z "$DEPS_DIR" ] && [ -f "$BUILD_DIR/CMakeCache.txt" ]; then
    DEPS_DIR=$(sed -n 's/^DEP_BUILD_DIR:[A-Z]*=//p' "$BUILD_DIR/CMakeCache.txt")
fi
if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then
    ARCH=$(uname -m)
    DEPS_DIR="${DEPS_DIR:-deps/build/$ARCH}"
    BUILD_DEPS_CMD="./build_release_macos.sh -d -a $ARCH"
else
    DEPS_DIR="${DEPS_DIR:-deps/build}"
    BUILD_DEPS_CMD="./build_linux.sh -d"
fi
case "$DEPS_DIR" in
    /*) ;;
    *) DEPS_DIR="$ROOT/$DEPS_DIR" ;;
esac

if [ ! -d "$DEPS_DIR/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" ]; then

content.text:
I checked the fixed build in the real app against staging, and both displays now update. clang-tidy also passes after one added include (commit 29801edb15). Nothing is pushed. To your first question: yes, the fix was case by case, and reading the code I found one gap it still leaves open.

**Was the fix case by case?** Yes. The app keeps five separate copies of the signed-in account and its credits, and each one asks the server on its own schedule:
- Home's AI card.
- The project's AI panel.
- The Preferences window.
- The printer chat that opens on Home.
- The JusPrin 1 import window.

Today, every place that changes the balance has to remember to tell the other copies. The code is full of such hand-written calls; one comment literally says "Both chats' balances are read again after." My fix added two more of these calls. Reading the code, I found one route it still misses:
- On Home, someone opens a printer's chat and sends a message, which spends credits.
- They close the chat and are back on Home.
- Home's card still shows the old balance. The app never counted the printer chat as "leaving Home", so the refresh I added never runs.

I haven't run this route yet, so treat it as unconfirmed.

**Decision needed:** should I replace the five copies with one shared copy before this goes out?
- **The proposal:** one object in the app holds the email and balance. It asks the server again on the events that can change them: a chat message finishing in any panel, a sign-in or sign-out anywhere, closing the credits purchase page, or the window regaining focus. Every screen draws from it and redraws when it changes. A new screen then can't forget to tell the others, because there are no others.
- **A guard:** a test that fails if anything other than that object asks the server for the account. The shell harness would also spend credits in each panel and check that every display shows the same number.
- **The cost:** changes to the AI panel's backend, Home's backend and the shell, all in JusPrin's own code, so no upstream files are touched. The alternative is to push the current fix and patch the printer-chat route with one more hand-written call.

My pick is the shared copy, done in this branch.

**Screen access:** you granted it this time, and the real-app check passed against staging:
- **Credits:** Home showed 493. I spent one credit on the server, which then said 492. After a new project and back to Home, the card showed 492.
- **Sign-out:** in Preferences, "Sign out" worked, and after the window closed Home no longer showed "Signed in as k+stg-e2e1@obico.io".

**clang-tidy:** it's the automatic check that blocks a pull request when a file uses something without including the header that declares it. It matters because CI runs it on every pull request, and it did find a real problem: the file used `std::move` without including `<utility>`, so the pull request would have failed. I ran it with the exact version CI uses, copied from another worktree, and it passes now.

**AI section after sign-out:** after you sign out, Home's right column shows only Printers, with no AI section and no way to sign back in from Home. I think this is a bug:
- The code's own description says Home shows the "Set up AI" options "while no agent is set up".
- But the test it uses is a flag that is set the first time AI is set up and never cleared on sign-out.
- So someone who signs out and has no API key can't use AI, yet Home behaves as if AI is ready.

The fix would show "Set up AI" whenever there's no sign-in, no API key and no connected AI tool. It's a small change in Home's backend plus a harness check. I can fold it into the same branch if you agree.

The screenshots from the staging check are in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/f7445e00-c658-4503-ada4-06ca44c57162/scratchpad/evidence/`.

input.ask: Build the account handling on the read-when-shown rule in this branch?

content.text:
Yes, I understand. The real problem isn't that several screens repeat the same call. It's that the app has no rule for when a balance on screen still matches the server. Each screen keeps its own copy, and other code has to remember to refresh it. My earlier proposal fixed the copying but still relied on refreshing after a list of events. That can't be complete, for the reason in the first fact below.

**What the design has to respect (facts from the code):**
- **The server is the only true source for credits, and the balance changes in places the app never sees.**
  - Someone buys credits in the browser.
  - Someone chats on another computer.
  - Sign-up credits expire on their date.
  - A plan's monthly credits renew.
  
  So any design built on "refresh after these events" will sometimes show a stale number.
- **The source for who is signed in is the settings file on this computer.** Only the app's own sign-in and sign-out code writes it.

**Proposal (not built):**
- **The rule:** a screen never shows a balance that wasn't read from the server for this time it's on screen. It reads when it comes on screen. While it stays on screen, it reads again:
  - after anything in the app that spends or adds credits: a chat message finishing in any panel, or the purchase page closing;
  - when the app window comes back to the front, which covers browser purchases and other computers.
- **While a read is in progress:** the screen keeps the last number read for the same account and replaces it when the answer comes. It never shows another account's number.
- **One module owns the account:** the server call, the last answer, which email that answer belongs to, and telling screens when it changes. A screen only says "I'm on screen" or "I'm off screen" and draws what the module gives it. No screen calls the server or reads the sign-in token itself, and a test fails if one does.
- **Where this pattern comes from:** web data libraries such as React Query and SWR work the same way. They re-fetch when a view appears and when the window regains focus, and they mark data stale after a change.
- **Left out on purpose:** timed polling, and the server pushing changes to the app. The only case they would add is a purchase on another computer while this window stays in front the whole time.

**Decision needed:** should I build account handling on this rule, in this branch, before pushing? It replaces the hand-written refresh calls across Home's backend, the AI panel's backend and the shell. """What GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account answers: numbers and names, so the app can
keep reading it for years, and the few sentences about money the app shows word
for word, so no price or plan wording is in the app's code."""
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Count, Sum
from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone

from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .billing import obico_premium
from .ledger import active_v2_plan, ensure_lots, live_lots
from .models import ChatTitle, CreditCharge, CreditGrant
from .reports import report_activity

USAGE_DAYS = 30


def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    return {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }


def _dollars(cents: int) -> str:
    return f'${cents // 100}' if cents % 100 == 0 else f'${cents / 100:.2f}'


def discounted_cents(cents: int) -> int:
    return cents * (100 - settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT) // 100


def _price_line(spec: Dict, obico_discount: bool) -> str:
    if not obico_discount:
        return f"{_dollars(spec['cents'])} a month."
    percent = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT
    return f"{_dollars(discounted_cents(spec['cents']))} a month with Obico Premium’s {percent}% off."


def _plan(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    obico_discount = obico_premium(user)
    return {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': obico_discount,
        'auto_reload': False,
        'price_line': _price_line(spec, obico_discount),
    }


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    # The title the app last sent for each chat (ChatTitle); None for a chat it
    # never sent one for.
    titles = dict(ChatTitle.objects.filter(user=user, chat_id__in={row['chat_id'] for row in rows if row['chat_id']})
                  .values_list('chat_id', 'title'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'title': titles.get(row['chat_id']),
                 'tier': row['tier'], 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity += report_activity(user, now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def remember_chat_title(user_id: int, chat_id: str, title: str) -> None:
    """Keeps the title the app sent with a chat's request, for naming that
    chat's usage. Writes only when the title changed."""
    title = ' '.join(title.split())[:ChatTitle._meta.get_field('title').max_length]
    if not title:
        return
    if not ChatTitle.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, chat_id=chat_id).exclude(title=title).update(title=title):
        ChatTitle.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, chat_id=chat_id, defaults={'title': title})


def _delete_warning(user, plan: Optional[Dict], credits: int) -> str:
    """What Delete account's confirmation says."""
    left = f"{credits:,} credit{'' if credits == 1 else 's'} left on {user.email} {'is' if credits == 1 else 'are'}"
    if plan and credits:
        gone = f"Your {plan['name']} plan ends today, and the {left} removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account."
    elif plan:
        gone = f"Your {plan['name']} plan ends today, and everything JusPrin keeps for {user.email} is removed."
    elif credits:
        gone = f'The {left} removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account.'
    else:
        gone = f'Everything JusPrin keeps for {user.email} is removed.'
    return f'{gone} This can\u2019t be undone.'


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or lot.expires_at is not None]
    total = sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots)
    plan = _plan(user)
    return {
        'credits': {'total': total, 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': plan,
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
        'delete_warning': _delete_warning(user, plan, total),
    }

input.ask: Build the version where each screen reads when shown, with no change notices?

content.text:
I reverted the sign-out change. The worktree is back to the two commits (4da941e553 and 29801edb15), and I rebuilt the app from them. On cost: one account read is cheap for the server (measured on staging below). On complexity: the design can avoid change notices entirely, so there's no reactive machinery to build.

**Is it complicated?** It doesn't have to be. Two ways to build it:

- **With change notices:** one class holds the last answer and the email it belongs to. If a second request comes in while a read is still in progress, it waits for that read instead of starting another. Screens register a callback to hear about changes. The native code already uses this kind of callback list, for example where it tells listeners that a slice request was declined. So it's about 80 lines, not a new framework. The AI pages already just draw what the native side sends, so they wouldn't change.
- **Without change notices (simpler):** reading the code, the screens that show credits are never on screen together:
  - Home and the project's AI panel are on different tabs.
  - The printer chat replaces both of them.
  - Preferences is a window that blocks the main window while it's open.

  So each screen can just read the account when it comes on screen and again after its own chats finish. "Comes on screen" includes the main window becoming active again after Preferences or the purchase page closes. No screen ever has to tell another. What remains shared is one read function that also checks the answer belongs to the account signed in now.

I'd build the second. It meets your rule that the server is the source of truth and every showing reads from it. The one-display-at-a-time point comes from reading the code; I haven't checked it in the running app.

**How often would it call the server?**
- About once each time a credits screen comes on screen.
- Once after each chat message finishes, which happens today already.
- Once each time the app window comes back to the front.

Today each AI page also reads again whenever its web view gets keyboard focus, which may be every click from the 3D view into the chat. I haven't measured that. The proposal would replace it with a read when the window comes back to the front, which should be fewer calls.

**Is the API cheap enough?** I measured the account read on staging for the test account. These timings come from an account with only 4 charges in the last 30 days:
- **Server work:** 9 database queries and about 9 ms (median of 20 runs, worst 21 ms).
- **Round trip from this Mac:** about 95 ms.
- **Answer size:** 1.2 KB.

Most of the work is the 30-day usage summary that the Billing and usage page shows. Its queries use an index on user and date. They grow with how much someone chats, but stay within one person's last 30 days of charges.

As a rough estimate, not a measurement: 1,000 people active at once, each causing one read a minute, comes to about 17 reads a second, or roughly 0.15 seconds of server work per second.

If heavy chatters ever make it costly, the server could answer a "balance only" request that skips the usage summary. That would be a change in tsd-enterprise, and I don't think it's needed now.
Yes, build that

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent**

The parent session local_2e8b84da gave the original task: fix two stale account displays on JusPrin 2's Home page, reproduce against staging (jusprinv2-stg.obico.io, not production), and work on a branch from jusprin-dev. Ask Kenneth before pushing. Shared notes folder: `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_2e8b84da-58b4-4ef1-bd87-b76f805fdf4d` (the note `home-account-card-fix.md` there has been updated).

That work produced two commits on `claude/home-account-refresh` (worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/home-account-refresh`). Neither is pushed:
- 4da941e553: the case-by-case fix.

Kenneth then asked:
- whether the fix was case-by-case and how to prevent this class of problem;
- to ask for screen access again (done; the real-app check passed);
- what clang-tidy is (explained; it now runs and passes);
- about the AI section after sign-out.

My proposed sign-out change (Home shows "Set up AI" when no AI is usable) was **rejected and reverted** on Kenneth's instruction.

Kenneth stressed the design should be a consistency mechanism, with the backend as the source of truth and screens reading when shown. He asked about complexity, call frequency and server cost. I answered:
- **Complexity:** the native code already uses callback lists, and the simpler variant needs no change notices at all.
- **Server cost (measured on staging):** 9 queries, about 9 ms of server work, about 95 ms round trip, 1.2 KB answer.

Kenneth approved: **"Yes, build that"**. That means building the version where each credits screen reads the account from the server whenever it comes on screen, with no cross-screen refresh calls. Pushing still needs Kenneth's explicit yes.

Standing constraints:
- Never push without Kenneth's yes.
- Never commit submodules.
- Ask before revert, reset or amend.
- No fix without reproduction.
- Builds use -j4, one per build directory, started in their own process group.
- Temporary docs stay untracked.
- Use the gcloud service account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
- No attribution lines in commits or PRs.
- Communication style:
  - Full sentences, no invented labels.
  - Decisions asked in full, starting with "Decision needed".
  - Report outcomes in under about 500 words.
  - Mark proposals as proposals.
  - Plain output style for a cold reader.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**

- Credits' only source of truth is the server's GET `/ent/jusprin/v2/account`. Credits change in places the app can't see: browser purchases, other computers, lots expiring, plan renewals. So screens read when they come on screen, never on notices from other screens.
- Who is signed in lives in the settings file: `jusprin_agent.jusprin_api_key` and `jusprin_agent.jusprin_account`.
- `IChatModelSource::fetch_account` is implemented by `AppConfigChatModelSource` in AgentConfiguration.cpp. It is the shared read, and it now drops answers for a token that changed while the read was in flight.
- Credit screens:
  - Home's AI card (`OrcaHomeBackend`);
  - the project AI panel (`AgentPane` → `AgentHost`);
  - the printer chat (`PrinterPanel::host()`);
  - Preferences (its own window, whose JS focus listeners are kept);
  - the import window (no chat, no credits).
- Triggers for a read:
  - main frame `wxEVT_ACTIVATE` (active). Verified on macOS: it fires when Preferences closes and when the app returns from hidden; the app-wide wxEVT_ACTIVATE_APP also fires but is not used;
  - Home tab shown;
  - agent pane expanded;
  - printer chat closed (`restore_task_panel`);
  - an AgentHost's own turn end and handshake (existing).
- Orca's MainFrame already binds wxEVT_ACTIVATE with Skip(). The shell binds its own handler, so no upstream file is touched.
- The shell harness `StandInGateway` records requests. Account reads are counted per event.

3. **Files and Code Sections**

All under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless noted. The changes are uncommitted in the worktree, together with temp debug lines.

- **Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp, `AppConfigChatModelSource::fetch_account`**: captures the token and passes the answer on only while that token is still saved.
  ```cpp
  const std::string token = load_provider_api_key(m_config, provider);
  Agent::fetch_account(*profile, token, endpoint_for(m_config, *profile), m_cancelled,
                       [post = m_post, done = std::move(done), config = m_config, provider,
                        token](std::optional<nlohmann::json> account) {
                           post([done, account = std::move(account), config, provider, token]() mutable {
                               // The account signed out, or another signed in, while this
                               // was read: the answer is not the one signed in now.
                               if (load_provider_api_key(config, provider) == token)
                                   done(std::move(account));
                           });
                       });
  ```

- **Agent/AgentHost.hpp**:
  - The AccountDone comment gains "An answer for an account signed out since is never given."
  - `void refresh_account();` is now declared, not inline, with the comment "Reads the signed-in account's credits and plan again, and a model list that failed, as the page's refresh_account does: each time the window showing this page comes on screen, since they change where the app cannot see."

- **Agent/AgentHost.cpp**:
  - The kRefreshAccount handler is now `else if (type == Protocol::kRefreshAccount) refresh_account();`.
  - New function:
  ```cpp
  void AgentHost::refresh_account()
  {
      request_account();
      // A model list that failed is asked again with it: Try again on an
      // account whose AI was unavailable, or coming back to the window.
      if (m_model_source)
          request_model_lists();
  }
  ```

- **Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp, `request_account`**: the callback is now `[this](std::optional<nlohmann::json> account) { // One that could not be read keeps the last answer. if (!account) return; m_account = ...; m_onboarding_changed = true; }`. The email capture was removed because the source now does that check. `follow_account` and `refresh_account` are unchanged, as is `#include <utility>` from commit 29801edb15.

- **Shell/ShellController.hpp**: added `void on_frame_activate(wxActivateEvent& event);` and `void read_account_on_screen();` with the comment "Whatever in the main window shows credits reads them from the server each time it comes on screen. The server is the only place they are true, and they change where the app cannot see (a purchase in the browser, a chat on another computer, a lot expiring), so a screen is never told by another that they changed."

- **Shell/ShellController.cpp**:
  - `frame.Bind(wxEVT_ACTIVATE, &ShellController::on_frame_activate, this);` with a matching `m_frame->Unbind(...)`.

input.content:
Credits: each screen reads the account from the server when it comes on screen

Credits change in places the app cannot see: a purchase in the browser,
a chat on another computer, a credit lot expiring. Until now each screen
was refreshed by whichever other screen happened to know it had changed,
so Home kept a stale balance after the printer chat spent credits or
after the app came back from the browser.

Now the server is the only source of truth, and whatever in the main
window shows credits reads GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account each time it
comes on screen: when the main window is activated (back from another
app, Preferences or the purchase page), when Home is shown, when the
project's AI panel is expanded, and when the printer chat closes. The
screen that is visible does the read; nothing tells another screen to
refresh. Preferences keeps its own page's read when its window gets
focus.

The shared account read now drops an answer for a token that is no
longer saved, so a read that was in flight when the person signed out
cannot put the old account back on Home.

Removed: the project panel page's own window-focus refresh, the
purchase sheet's refresh of the agent pane, and Preferences' refresh of
Home and the main window's pane; the main window's activation covers
them.

The shell harness counts account requests per step: one read each when
moving between a project's tabs, returning to Home, closing the printer
chat and reactivating the window.
